steps.text: Wash and pick over cranberries. Place in a medium saucepan with water, and sugar. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, stir and simmer for 10 minutes or until cranberries burst.
Slightly mash the cranberries with the back of a wooden spoon to insure all skins are broken. Add the cinnamon, nutmeg and allspice. Mix well.
Remove from heat and mix in the blueberries (don't be afraid to break a few, but don't over mash either). The sauce will thicken as it cools.
Transfer to a bowl, cool slightly and place plastic wrap directly on top of sauce to cover. Refrigerate until chilled.

raw_recipe.headline: Blueberry Cranberry Sauce
raw_recipe.description: A pint of fresh blueberries is incorporated into this recipe for a traditional cranberry sauce made from scratch. This sauce can be made a day or two ahead.

review.reviewBody: This is wonderful! I added a bit more sugar and used half fresh blueberries and half fresh raspberries. It not only tasted great, but looked beautiful. My kids ate it alone, without the turkey and asked for more until it was gone. A huge hit.

Giving it 5 stars even though it was very runny, which might have been due to how I cooked the cranberries. I didn't want any skins so I strained the mashed cranberries and put the remaining skins and flesh in my food processor before putting back in the bowl with the juice. I added equal parts of blueberries and raspberries. I also used orange juice for the water as per other reviewers. Everyone LOVED the flavor and put it on the rolls, ice cream, pancakes, etc. Thanksgiving and the following four days. I will make this again but try to get it a little thicker.

This sauce always gets rave reviews from my family. My sister requested I make my cranberry relish again this year. So I am. Some years I use the blueberries, other years I've used mixed berries, raspberries or blackberries. But I love the suggestion to use 1 cup of O.J. in lieu of the water, then add some zest of 1 orange. This year I'm going to mix in some actual orange to the sauce with the fresh blueberries after it cools. 
I love this recipe because there is so much you can do with it!

I made it a little differently... I put equal amounts of fresh cranberries and fresh blueberries, well rinsed (make sure to pick out any that aren't up to best quality). I don't add any spices. But, I do add 1 - 2 tsp. of fresh orange zest. And a full cup of sugar. I stirred and mashed the berries as they cooked. We like to fix it in advance and chill in the refrigerator. It is great with turkey, or ham. But, it is also good over cottage cheese, or mix a spoonful into a cup of plain or vanilla yogurt.

Every time I serve this there are rave reviews and requests for the recipe. Because a number of people have pre-diabetes/diabetes, I substitute Splenda for the white sugar. I made the mistake of substituting Stevia once...DON'T do it!! When you heat Stevia it becomes bitter.

after cooking the cranberries i drained off some of the liquid. i added frozen blue berries still frozen to the still warm cranberry sauce, i omitted the allspice since i didn't have any. i did a taste test adding sugar til the tangy wasn't so strong. This was so delicious i made a piece of toast and had this on it.
This was fabulous and will be my go-to cranberry sauce recipe going forward! I did follow the other reviewers comments and upped the sugar to 3/4 cup.

I followed the directions on the cranberry bag 1 cup water and 1 cup sugar. I added the spices and when the cranberries were cooked I added 1 cup blueberries and 1 cup raspberries. Came out great. Will definitely make this again.

Great...This is even better the next day with sliced white turkey, dressing and mayo on pumpernickel bread, as a sandwich you can not beat it. Did use Splenda, instead of sugar,(1 cup),cinnamon (2t) and orange juice instead of water.

Betty Parker
I skipped thw white sugar and used honey (1/4 cup). The spices are perfect. This wonderful on pancakes! You could always add a little orange or more blueberries instead of sugar.
This is the best cranberry sauce ever. I made it for Thanksgiving dinner and for turkey sandwiches the next few days. The only thing I changed was, I used one cup of Splenda sugar.
I added a splash of key lime juice to the water for boiling cranberries.
I love this recipe. I’ve had requests for it even. No changes! Follow the directions, it comes out great.
Excellent recipe! As many suggested, I added extra sugar. It is beautiful, smells wonderful, & is delicious! This will be a new standard at our house! Thank you!!
This is absolutely delicious cranberry sauce. One thing I would suggest is instead of using water use orange juice!
Delicious!

We’ve been making this for Thanksgiving and fall time for around 10 years now I would say and my family loves it! My kids specifically ask for it. Such a nice twist to straight cranberry sauce. Thank you for such a great recipe!
This has become my go-to cranberry recipe for Thanksgiving. The blueberries are perfect to balance out the tartness of the cranberries. It’s a favorite!
I added pecans.
I personally leave out the all-spice but otherwise love this recipe and make it for feasts every year.
